title: Math Class and Numeric Operations

understand.concept: System.Math provides static methods and constants for common mathematical operations. Examples include Abs, Max, Min, Pow, Sqrt, Floor, Ceiling, Round and PI. The overload chosen depends on argument types; decimal and double overloads have different precision and behavior. Math.Round uses midpoint-to-even by default for relevant overloads, while an explicit MidpointRounding mode can request another policy. Math methods do not remove the need to check domain, range and precision.
understand.whyItMatters: The Math API provides tested building blocks for geometry, pricing rules, statistics and scientific calculations.
understand.analogy: System.Math is like a well-stocked mathematics toolkit, with named tools for common calculations.
understand.analogyLimit: Floating-point results can be approximate. Rounding policy must be chosen deliberately for financial or domain-specific rules; Math does not automatically enforce business constraints.

explain.narrative:
## Common Math methods

`Math.Abs` returns an absolute value; `Math.Max` and `Math.Min` select the larger or smaller value; `Math.Pow` calculates a power; and `Math.Sqrt` calculates a square root. `Math.PI` provides the value of pi.

## Rounding and integer boundaries

`Math.Floor` rounds toward negative infinity and `Math.Ceiling` toward positive infinity. `Math.Round` rounds to a specified number of fractional digits; its default midpoint behavior is to-even for the relevant overloads. Select `MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero` when that policy is required by the domain.

## Numeric type and precision

Math offers overloads for numeric types, but many common methods use double. Use decimal for decimal business values where appropriate, and understand when converting to double changes precision. Validate input domains, such as non-negative values for square roots in real-number calculations.

Examples target .NET 10 and C# 14.
